issues.legal_issue: A later eviction proceeding based on bona fide requirement is not barred by the rule against reopening finally decided issues when the earlier proceeding was disposed of without deciding any issue.
material_facts: The landlord's earlier eviction proceeding was not pressed and was disposed of without a decision on the merits.
The landlord later initiated another eviction proceeding against the occupant of the same premises based on a bona fide requirement.
issues.conclusion: The finality provision did not bar the later proceeding because no issue had been finally decided in the earlier proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 45 of the Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961, incorporates principles of res judicata and permits summary rejection only where proceedings involve the same parties or their privies and substantially the same issues have been finally decided in a former proceeding. Because the earlier proceeding was disposed of without deciding any issue, the provision did not apply.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction under a rent-control regime.
predicates.same_parties_or_privies: The successive proceedings involve the same parties or persons claiming under them.
predicates.former_proceeding_disposed_without_decis: The earlier proceeding was disposed of without deciding any issue.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding under a rent-control regime is brought between the same parties or their privies after an earlier proceeding ended without a decision on any issue, the later proceeding is not barred by finality.

issues.legal_issue: Withdrawing an eviction proceeding without permission does not bar a later proceeding based on a recurring bona fide requirement that is assessed as of the later proceeding.
material_facts: The landlord withdrew an earlier eviction proceeding without seeking permission to file a fresh proceeding.
The later proceeding concerned the same premises but relied on the landlord's current need for a larger office, which was assessed as of the date of the later proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The withdrawal rule did not bar the later eviction proceeding because the current bona fide requirement was a recurring cause and the cause of action could differ despite the premises being the same.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXIII Rule 1(4)(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure precludes a fresh suit concerning the same subject matter after withdrawal without permission. Subject matter is not merely the property; it includes the cause of action and the relief claimed. In eviction proceedings based on bona fide requirement, the requirement is assessed as of the date of the suit and may recur. The Court relied on Vallabh Das v. Dr. Madanlal, K.S. Sundararaju Chettiar v. M.R. Ramachandra Naidu, and Surajmal v. Radhe Shyam.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_proceeding and prior_claim_withdrawn_without_permission and same_premises and recurring_bona_fide_requirement and later_claim_based_on_current_need

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a tenant's eviction.
predicates.prior_claim_withdrawn_without_permission: The claimant withdrew an earlier claim without obtaining permission to bring a fresh proceeding.
predicates.same_premises: The earlier and later claims concern the same premises.
predicates.recurring_bona_fide_requirement: The eviction ground is a bona fide requirement that can recur over time.
predicates.later_claim_based_on_current_need: The later claim relies on the claimant's need assessed at the time of the later proceeding.

issues.definition: When an eviction claim concerning the same premises is brought after an earlier claim was withdrawn without permission, a later claim based on a current, recurring bona fide requirement is not barred by the withdrawal.
